text:
A test-tube contains 1.0cm3 of liquid water at 100°C. The liquid water boils to form 1600cm3 of
steam.
What is the reason for the large increase in volume?
A
Steam molecules are bigger than water molecules.
B
The average distance between the molecules is much greater in the steam.
C
The molecules do not move until the water turns into a gas.
D
There are more steam molecules than there were water molecules.

options.label: A
options.text: Steam molecules are bigger than water molecules.

options.label: B
options.text: The average distance between the molecules is much greater in the steam.

options.label: C
options.text: The molecules do not move until the water turns into a gas.

options.label: D
options.text: There are more steam molecules than there were water molecules.
